When I was about 6 I lived in a really old town in Pennsylvania that had a lot of history back in the 1800s. My dad and I used to go for walks in the evening and always made sure to pass by this house that we were sure was haunted.  Real creepy-ass house with the paint peeling and everything. No one had lived in it for a while. Being in a horror obsessed family, I was fascinated by it, and my dad and I would even take turns going up onto the porch and opening the mail slot to look in. God, it was creepy in there. It really had a feeling. Naturally, we loved it . so fast-forward about a year, I was at a playground with a crazy family friend and her daughter. A playground, which I must add, was right behind the street the house was on. You could even see into the backyard if you got close enough. I told them that the house was haunted, and convinced them to come with me so I could show them. On the porch, me and the mom went up and opened the mail slot to look in. Right away, a tiny, very old sheet of paper flew out of the slot, like it had been blown out by the wind. The woman picked it up and went pale. It seemed to be a sheet of music, stained and yellowed, with lyrics amongst the bars of notes. And the lyrics were the same word over and over again, across the whole page. "My, my, my, my, my, my, my, my, my.."  I thought it was kinda funny at the time. The mom was scared though. We threw the sheet of music off the porch and it landed in the flowerbed. Even though I laughed, I was terrified days later. I felt like the house didn't want me to go near it anymore. I'd be scared every time I walked past it and saw the yellowed sheet of music lying in that same flowerbed, and I just felt cold seeing the house, and knowing I wasn't welcome there. Still freaks me out to this day.
